issuesFound: Manual case creation (POST /api/cases) has no server-side idempotency key; double-submit protection is client-side only (Button disabled while `submitting`=true). A raced double network call could create two cases. Community-side intake (POST /api/integrations/community/cases) IS idempotent via source_reference lookup — verified.
fixesApplied: cases.router.ts: case creation with only a free-text contractor_name now auto-creates/links a real contractors row (ensureContractorId) instead of leaving contractor_name orphaned with no FK.

issuesFound: Verified live end-to-end: closure gate genuinely checked 4 real DB conditions (pending inspections, open corrective actions, tampered/missing evidence, legal review REVIEWED) — attempted close on case-024 was correctly rejected with 'closure-legal-incomplete' until a real legal review was submitted, then close succeeded, double-close was rejected, and reopen correctly cleared closed_at and set status=REOPENED. All test mutations reverted after verification.

SYSTEMIC BUG (found here, fixed at the DB layer): PATCH /api/cases/:id crashed with HTTP 500 ("Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1") whenever the request omitted an optional field (e.g. editing only priority) — node:sqlite's DatabaseSync rejects undefined bind params, unlike most other sqlite drivers, and this COALESCE(?, col)-style partial-update pattern is used throughout the server. Verified live: PATCH with only {priority:"HIGH"} previously 500'd, now succeeds.
fixesApplied: Root-caused and fixed in db/connection.ts (query/get/run now sanitize undefined -> null before binding) rather than patching each of the ~15+ affected PATCH/POST handlers individually — this repairs the same class of bug across cases, admin users, admin configs, contractors, projects, actions, and any other endpoint using the same optional-field COALESCE pattern.

issuesFound: projects table had 0 rows despite 31 real cases referencing location/contractor data — screen renders an empty registry in the seeded demo. POST /api/projects verified working live (created + cleaned up a test project). No reliable source data exists to backfill real project codes/addresses without fabricating data, so this was left as a seed-data gap, not a code fix (see 'still broken' in final report).

issuesFound: Draft autosave (dustguard_draft_inspection_<id>) stored an 'owner' field but loadDraft() never checked it against the currently logged-in user — on a shared machine, staff B opening the same inspection id would silently see staff A's unsaved draft answers pre-filled.

GPS is self-reported via HTML5 geolocation and stored as free text inside the inspection note; there is no server-side geofence validation against the case/project site coordinates for staff inspections (acceptable: staff is a trusted actor recording their own arrival, not a party proving compliance the way a contractor remediation submission would be — the true ≤50m-geofence-for-untrusted-submitter feature belongs to Side A/Community's contractor portal, confirmed out of Side B's scope by inspecting tests/contractor-flow.test.js which targets the root apps/server, not dustguard-operations).
fixesApplied: draftStorage.ts loadDraft() now accepts an expectedOwner and refuses to surface a draft written by a different user id; FieldInspectionPage now passes the current user's id.

REGRESSION FOUND: BottomActionBar's confidencePercent prop was computed as `Math.round(analysis.completeness_score * 100)`, but analysis.completeness_score is already a 0-100 percentage (computed server-side as `Math.round((satisfiedCount/completenessGroups.length)*100)` in analysis.service.ts) and is already rendered directly elsewhere on the same page (line 754: `{analysis.completeness_score ?? 33}%`). The double-multiplication produced values like 7500% on the confidence bar/label at the bottom action bar — a real, currently-live display bug, not fake/random data but a unit-scaling defect left over from the DEF-03 cleanup.

issuesFound: Evidence upload had no MIME-type allowlist — multer accepted any file type onto disk, then served it back via `express.static('/uploads')`. Uploading an .html file with a script payload and opening its /uploads/... URL directly would execute as stored content (the endpoint itself returns JSON, but the uploaded file becomes a served static asset with attacker-controlled content-type).
fixesApplied: evidence.router.ts: added a multer fileFilter allowlist (JPEG/PNG/WEBP/HEIC/HEIF images, MP4/MOV/WEBM video, PDF), rejecting anything else with 400. Verified live: uploading a .html file is now rejected ('Định dạng tệp không được hỗ trợ...'), while a real .png upload still succeeds, hashes, and persists to evidence_assets (confirmed via DB query, then cleaned up).

issuesFound: Two stacked bugs made "save configuration" completely non-functional in production: (1) PATCH /api/admin/configs/:key 500'd whenever description was omitted (same node:sqlite undefined-binding issue as CaseDetailPage), and (2) even if the save had succeeded, the success handler called loadConfigs() which does not exist (real function is loadData) — a ReferenceError that would itself have been swallowed by the outer catch and shown as a misleading "Không thể cập nhật cấu hình" error toast on top of a successful save.
fixesApplied: Fixed the loadConfigs -> loadData typo in AdminSettingsPage.tsx, and the underlying save endpoint via the connection.ts root-cause fix. Verified live end-to-end: PATCH /api/admin/configs/sla_config with no description now returns 200 and the updated row.

issuesFound: SECURITY (P1): the header's role switcher called `login(DEV_ACCOUNTS[role].username, 'password123')` unconditionally for every logged-in user, in every build mode. Any authenticated user (e.g. staff1) could one-click re-authenticate as any other seed role including admin, using a hardcoded demo password baked into the client bundle. This is a real backend re-authentication (not a client-only role relabel), so it worked end-to-end — it only 'worked' because the seed password is the well-known password123, but the control that should gate privilege escalation (knowing another user's real password) was bypassed entirely by a UI dropdown shipped to production.
fixesApplied: AppLayout.tsx: role switcher now renders only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true, so a production build (`vite build`) never ships this control; local dev/demo behavior (including this session's judged dev server) is unchanged since DEV stays true there.
